Theoretical Background
2.1
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
RAG bridges the gap between the static knowledge of a pre-trained language model and
dynamic, domain-specific data. The pipeline consists of two distinct phases:
1. The Ingestion Phase: During ingestion, raw documents are parsed to extract
raw text. This text is typically too long to fit into a neural network’s context window,
so it is split into overlapping "chunks" (e.g., 500 words each). A specialized embedding
model (such as all-MiniLM-L6-v2) processes each chunk and outputs a high-dimensional
vector (an array of floating-point numbers) representing the semantic meaning of that
chunk. These vectors are stored in a specialized Vector Database.
2. The Retrieval & Generation Phase: When a user submits a query, the query
itself is passed through the same embedding model to generate a query vector. The Vector
Database computes the mathematical distance (e.g., Cosine Similarity or L2 distance)
between the query vector and all document chunk vectors.
2.2
